correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs Ardila's vertex coordinates exactly. The special expanded pair is adjacent, so its two odd labels differ by \(2\); this gives \(\|v_B\|^2=2n(4n^2-1)/3+2s^2+4s\). The first/second-occurrence pattern is a Dyck word and \(s=2A-n^2\). Every staircase partition size occurs, so every area level is realized. The squared norm is strictly ordered on the full allowed \(s\)-range. Uniqueness of the Euclidean minimum enclosing ball plus the published simultaneous \(S_n\)-symmetry forces its center to be the origin. The finite checker independently corroborates the algebra and enumerations through bounded sizes but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The bipermutahedron is a canonical high-symmetry polytope arising in the Lagrangian geometry of matroids. Its published realization is not vertex-transitive and is not centrally symmetric for \(n\ge3\), so an exact metric collapse is not automatic. The theorem compresses all vertex norms to one Catalan/Dyck-area statistic, gives the complete set of distinct radial shells in every dimension, and identifies the exact circumradius and outer-shell multiplicity. These are natural intrinsic data of the canonical realization and supply a concrete bridge between its Euclidean and Catalan combinatorics.
